lines.text: My garage door just stopped halfway down and went back up. It only does that when something is *in the way.*
It started at a red light. At night, most lights don't run on a timer. They wait for a loop of wire under the road to feel the *metal* of a car.
That's why bikes get stuck at red lights. They're too small for the loop to notice.
It's 3 a.m. I'm the only car at the intersection. Then the light for the empty side street turns *green.*
Nobody's there. But the loop feels something. Something big. Made of *metal.* With its lights off.
Then the turn arrow beside me goes green. The lane beside me is empty.
But I can hear an engine. *Idling.* Right outside my window.
My light turns green. I floor it.
Every light on the way home is already green when I get there. Every single one.
My mirror stays empty the whole way. But at every corner, I hear it. *One car length back.*
I pull into my garage and hit the button. Garage doors have a little beam across the bottom. If anything breaks it, the door goes back up.
Halfway down, my door stops. And rolls back up.
I turn off my engine. The garage goes quiet.
Except in the empty half of my garage, *another engine* is still running.
